en: At the time when the earth turned hot,
at the time when the heavens turned about,
at the time when the sun was darkened
the time of the rise of the Pleiades, the night,
the slime, this was the source of the earth,
the source of deepest darkness, that made darkness,
the source of Night, that made night,
the intense darkness, the deep darkness,
darkness of the sun, darkness of the night,
notes: The opening of the first of the chant's sixteen eras (wā); the whole runs to more than 2,000 lines, through the births of sea creatures paired with land plants, the coming of day and the human genealogies.
Line 5: Makaliʻi, the Pleiades, whose rising opens the Hawaiian year.
The chant was printed in 1889 under King Kalākaua; Queen Liliʻuokalani published an English translation in 1897.
